skill.name: tasks-generator
skill.description: Generate implementation task roadmaps from PRDs, technical specifications, and UI/UX documents, including sprint structure, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and verification steps.
skill.summary: Turns product and technical specifications into sprint-based task plans with dependencies and verification steps.
skill.author: Emz1998

content.value_statement: Project teams often struggle to turn specifications into clear implementation work. This skill converts specs into phased tasks with dependencies and verification steps.
actual_capabilities: Extracts tasks from PRDs, technical specifications, and UI/UX specifications.
Organizes work into foundation, build, and deployment phases.
Marks independent tasks that can run in parallel.
Adds acceptance criteria and verification guidance for each sprint.
Identifies dependencies, critical paths, risks, and blockers.
limitations: Requires useful source specifications or user-provided context.
Does not estimate team capacity from live project data.
Does not execute project commands or validate the generated tasks.
May need manual review for complex organizational constraints.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Build
use_cases.description: Convert a PRD and technical plan into sequenced sprints for a new application.

use_cases.title: Prepare Engineering Implementation Work
use_cases.description: Break architecture, API, and UI requirements into testable tasks for developers.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Delivery
use_cases.description: Find independent frontend, backend, and testing tasks that can start at the same time.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Task Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one specification document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a task roadmap from this PRD. Include phases, sprints, task IDs, acceptance criteria, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build from Multiple Specs
prompt_templates.scenario: Use product, technical, and design documents together.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the PRD, tech specs, and UI/UX specs. Create a sprint plan with dependencies and parallel task markers.

prompt_templates.title: Refine for Team Execution
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an existing plan for engineering delivery.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this task plan. Split oversized tasks, add missing tests, identify blockers, and improve dependency sequencing.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Complex Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a larger implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a detailed roadmap with critical path analysis, cross-sprint dependencies, risk mitigations, and suggested subagent allocation.

output_examples.input: A PRD for a note-taking application with authentication, offline drafts, and sync.
output_examples.output: A phased roadmap with setup, type definitions, auth tasks, editor tasks, sync work, tests, and deployment checks.

output_examples.input: Technical specs for an API migration and UI redesign.
output_examples.output: A sprint plan that separates API contracts, migration work, UI components, integration tests, and release validation.

output_examples.input: An existing roadmap with unclear dependencies.
output_examples.output: A revised plan with blocked tasks, parallel opportunities, critical path notes, and clearer acceptance criteria.

best_practices: Provide the PRD, technical specs, and UI/UX specs together when possible.
Review generated dependencies with engineers before assigning sprint work.
Keep task size small enough for isolated implementation and testing.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague requirements and expect a precise implementation plan.
Do not skip manual review of risks, ownership, and team capacity.
Do not treat generated estimates as commitments without team validation.

faq.question: What documents should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a PRD, technical specifications, UI/UX specifications, or any document that describes features and constraints.

faq.question: Can it plan work without a PRD?
faq.answer: Yes, but the output will be less precise. Provide goals, features, constraints, and known dependencies.

faq.question: Does it run project commands?
faq.answer: No. It suggests verification steps, but command execution remains under user control.

faq.question: Can it mark parallel tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It marks tasks that do not depend on other tasks in the same sprint.

faq.question: Does it replace project management software?
faq.answer: No. It creates structured planning content that teams can copy into their preferred tools.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
